correctness.rationale: Kummer counts base-p subtraction borrows exactly. Removing r terminal base-p digits equal to p-1 repeats the reduced-row good/bad indicator p^r times. In reduced row N=m-1, Q=p^alpha and R=m mod Q (1<=R<Q), first R entries suffer fewer than alpha borrows. For any K with [K,K+R] inside row N, digitwise maximum Z of K mod Q with the digits of R lies in [K,K+R] and forces alpha consecutive borrows against the lowest alpha digits of N=R-1 mod Q. Thus every longer interval contains a multiple of p^alpha and both edge R-blocks attain the bound. All limits n>=0, prime p, alpha>=1 are addressed. Direct exact binomial verifier covers 8320 configurations and 1,221,990 forbidden windows; the infinite conclusion follows from the proof, not tests.

originality.rationale: The searched primary results of Fine, Rowland and Spiegelhofer-Wallner give counts and subword generating functions, not maximum consecutive nondivisibility runs. Kummer is a general pointwise valuation theorem, but does not state the all-parameter sharp covering extremum; the constructive maximum-digit witness proves this missing interval claim. An earlier exact statement in unlocated prime-power Pascal-row geometry remains a priority risk, particularly the detailed 1997 Granville survey that was identified but not materially inspected. Literature searches alone are not novelty proof.
residual_risks: Exact extremal identity may be explicitly stated in historical work under a different term or an equivalent p-adic digit condition.

Granville (1997), Arithmetic Properties of Binomial Coefficients I, is plausibly relevant and identified but not examined in full; its general digit congruence is not treated as a full-document negative comparison.
Prime-modulus special case may be known as an elementary consequence of Lucas; novelty claim is the uniform all-prime-power sharp covering theorem, not the elementary p-only case.

value.rationale: This is a natural extremal invariant for every row of Pascal’s triangle, complementing Fine/Rowland exact survivor counts with order-sensitive geometric information. The formula provides an immediate answer without binomial expansion for every prime power and row; stronger than a count, it supplies a uniform optimal hitting radius and a constructive divisible coefficient inside every overlong interval. The obstruction operates at arbitrary alpha and general p, and the two edge blocks prove sharpness. Motivated by the exact count literature and missing longest-run profile, not arbitrary finite slices. No downstream application is claimed as proved.
